_note: Hand-translated English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 3 (burning bush, divine name revelation, commissioning of Moses). The most theologically dense chapter so far — Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic interpretive moves are heavy. Key moves preserved: v.1 אמאם מדין = 'imām of Midian'; v.1 טרף אלברייה = 'the edge of the wilderness'; v.1 חריב = Horeb; v.2 מלך אללה = 'the angel of God' (Saadia for מלאך יהוה — uses Aramaic-derived מלאך for messenger); v.2 בצרים נאר = 'in a flame of fire'; v.2 אלסנא = 'the thornbush' (Saadia transliterates the Hebrew סנה in this recension — Cairo 2019; an alternate Saadia tradition has אלעוסג'); v.4 עלם אללה = 'God knew' (the standard Saadia rendering of וירא = knew); v.4 לביך = 'I am at your service' (Saadia's standard for הנני); v.5 מקדס = 'consecrated' (Saadia for קדש); v.6 נור אללה = 'the light of God' — MAJOR anti-anthropomorphic move: God has no 'face' to behold; Moses covers his face from God's LIGHT, not from God's countenance; v.7 גלאוזתהם = 'their oppressors / taskmasters' (Saadia for נגשים); v.8 פתגלית = 'and I appeared / I revealed myself' — second MAJOR move: Saadia rejects the literal 'I descended' (וארד) and substitutes appearing/manifestation; v.8 בלד יפיץ' אללבן ואלעסל = 'a land flowing with milk and honey'; v.14 אלאזלי אלד'י לא יזול = 'the Eternal who never ceases' — Saadia's philosophical interpretation of אהיה אשר אהיה: not 'I will be what I will be' but a name asserting God's timeless eternity; v.14 אלאזלי = 'the Eternal' as the operational divine name in this revelation; v.15 אלי' גיל ואגיאל = 'unto generation upon generation'; v.18 ואפאנא אמרה = 'His decree has come to us' (Saadia for נקרה עלינו); v.18 נד'בח ללה רבנא = 'offer sacrifice to the Lord our God'; v.20 אפאתי = 'my plagues / my calamities'; v.20 אעגובאתי = 'my wonders'; v.22 ותנתספו אלמצריון = 'and you shall divest the Egyptians' — Saadia takes the Hebrew ונצלתם not as 'rescue/save' but as 'strip/divest', preserving the unusual verb-sense.

translations.1: And Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the imām of Midian; and he led it to the edge of the wilderness, and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.
translations.2: And the angel of God appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of the thornbush. And he saw — and behold, the thornbush was blazing with fire, yet it was not being consumed.
translations.3: And Moses said: 'Let me turn aside now and see this wondrous sight — why the thornbush is not burning.'
translations.4: And God knew that he had turned aside to see; and He called to him from the thornbush, and said: 'Moses! Moses!' He said: 'I am at your service.'
translations.5: He said: 'Do not draw near hither; take off your sandals from your feet — for the place upon which you are standing is consecrated.'
translations.6: Then He said: 'I am the God of your father — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' And Moses covered his face, for he was afraid to look upon the light of God.
translations.7: And He said: 'I have looked upon the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their crying-out because of their taskmasters, and I have known their pains.
translations.8: So I have appeared, to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land — to a good and wide land, a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
translations.9: And now — behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has reached me; and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
translations.10: So come now, and I shall send you to Pharaoh; and bring out my people, the sons of Israel, from Egypt.'
translations.11: And Moses said before God: 'Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?'
translations.12: He said: 'I shall be with you; and this is the sign for you that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall worship God upon this mountain.'
translations.13: And Moses said before God: 'Behold, I am going to the sons of Israel, and I shall say to them: The God of your fathers has sent me to you. And they shall ask me: What is His name? — What shall I say to them?'
translations.14: He said to him: 'The Eternal who never ceases.' Then He said: 'Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel: The Eternal has sent me to you.'
translations.15: And He said to him further: 'Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel: The Lord, the God of your fathers — the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob — has sent me to you. This is My name forever, and this is My memorial unto generation upon generation.
translations.16: Go and gather the elders of the sons of Israel, and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers, has appeared to me — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — saying: I have remembered you, and what has been done to you in Egypt.
translations.17: And I have said: I shall bring you up from the torment of the Egyptians, to the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites — to a land flowing with milk and honey.
translations.18: And when they accept from you, you shall enter — you and the elders of the sons of Israel — to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him: The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has caused His decree to come upon us. So now — let us journey a distance of three days into the wilderness, and let us offer sacrifice to the Lord our God.
translations.19: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go — and not [even] under a single strong hand.
translations.20: So I shall send forth all my plagues, and shall strike the Egyptians with my wonders which I shall do among them; and after that he shall let you go.
translations.21: And I shall give this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians; so it shall be, when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.
translations.22: Rather, each woman shall ask as a gift from her [woman-]neighbor and from the dweller in her house — vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments; and you shall set them upon your sons and upon your daughters; and you shall divest the Egyptians.'
